title: Rewinding the input head
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $M$ be a Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet and states in $S$. Let $a,b\in S$ and let $d$ be an optional state. Suppose that, for every input symbol (including a blank) and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition from $a$ moves the input head left, leaves all work tapes and the output unchanged, and enters $b$. Suppose also that from $b$ the machine, on reading a Boolean symbol, moves the input head left and remains in $b$, while on reading a blank it moves right and enters $d$; in both cases it leaves all work tapes and the output unchanged. Then from every configuration $c$ on input $x$ whose state is $a$, there is a natural number $r\leq p+2$, where $p$ is the input-head position of $c$, such that after $r$ steps the configuration has state $d$ and input-head position $1$, with every other component equal to that of $c$. At every step count $u\leq r$, the work-tape head positions are the same as in $c$.
